exact_lemma: For any original full-D feasible probability law, let f be its first-coordinate marginal density. For each fixed0<|delta|<1, the set of x with0<f(x)<infinity and f(x+delta)=b*f(x) has Lebesgue measure zero. The reverse equality with b^(-1) is likewise impossible almost everywhere where f(x)>0. No common null set over uncountably many delta is asserted.
complete_argument: Absolute continuity is derived, not assumed. If A is any Lebesgue-null Borel subset of R2, integrate mu(A)<=b^(-1)mu(A+h) over h in D. Tonelli makes the right integral zero, since every translate of A is null. Therefore mu(A)=0 and a joint density p exists; its coordinate marginal f is integrable and finite almost everywhere.

Fix delta with0<|delta|<1 and t=(1-|delta|)/2>0. Both shifts(delta,0) and(delta,t) lie in D. The two density inequalities p(x+delta,y)>=b*p(x,y) and p(x+delta,y+t)>=b*p(x,y) hold almost everywhere in(x,y). Only these TWO fixed shifts are used, so Fubini gives one full-measure set of x on which both inequalities hold almost everywhere in y and the slices are integrable.

At any such x with0<f(x)<infinity and f(x+delta)=b*f(x), integrating either nonnegative difference gives zero. Thus p(x+delta,y)=b*p(x,y)=p(x+delta,y+t) almost everywhere in y. The nonnegative integrable slice g(y)=p(x+delta,y) is therefore t-periodic and has positive integral b*f(x). But an integrable nonnegative periodic function on R is zero almost everywhere: its integrals on all translated periods are equal, so a nonzero period integral would make the total infinite. Contradiction. Hence the equality set is null. Repeating with -delta proves the reverse strictness.
